overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the December 6 notice was properly posted at Town Hall, removing one public comment period was permitted, minutes need not be posted online, and the own-policy claim is outside the law. Resolved by informal action.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the December 6 meeting notice was not properly posted.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice for the December 6 meeting was properly posted in compliance with the Open Meeting Law where the Town Clerk posted both the original and amended notices more than 48 hours in advance in the official notice posting location, i.e. the bulletin board at Town Hall.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by amending the notice to remove one of two public comment periods.
allegations.key_passage: Nevertheless, the Committee allowed public participation towards the end of its meeting after it discussed the open session topics and heard from three individuals, including the complainant.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to post meeting minutes on its website.
Complainant alleged the committee violated its own public comment policy, which is not part of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.
